full_text_en:
Cai Zengxiong v. Gongbei Customs — appeal against administrative penalty

Appellant: Cai Zengxiong, male, 52 years old, from Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, captain of the Taiwan-registered cargo vessel "Guangda No. 2", residing at No. 11, Lane 90, Dengshan Street, Kaohsiung City, Taiwan Province.
Agent ad litem: Ye Qing, Ye Naifu, lawyers of Guangdong Nanyue Law Firm.
Appellee: Gongbei Customs of the People's Republic of China.
Legal representative: Yang Junsheng, Director of Gongbei Customs.
Agent ad litem: Xu Zuopu, Senior Customs Supervisor of Gongbei Customs.
Agent ad litem: Luo Pinglong, lawyer of Zhuhai Law Firm.

Appellant Cai Zengxiong, in the case of being subjected to administrative penalty by Gongbei Customs for smuggling cigarettes, being dissatisfied with the administrative judgment (1989) Zhu Zhong Fa Xing Shen Zi No. 1 of the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, filed an appeal with the Guangdong High People's Court on October 16, 1989. The court formed a collegial panel according to law and, upon trial, found the following facts:

In the early morning of March 3, 1989, a customs anti-smuggling vessel of Gongbei Customs intercepted and stopped the cargo vessel "Guangda No. 2" at a location within China's internal waters at longitude 114°35′45″ east, latitude 22°10′50″ north, i.e., the sea area near Dangan Island, Zhuhai City. The vessel had a deadweight tonnage of 3,000 tons, a crew of 31 persons, and the holds contained 500 tons of scrap iron and 500 tons of porcelain clay. On the deck were stacked 4,760 cases (238,000 cartons) of foreign-brand cigarettes such as "555" and "Kent", specially packed in sealed plastic bags. The cargo manifest carried on board only listed the quantities of scrap iron and porcelain clay, with no record of the 4,760 cases of cigarettes. On March 11, 1989, pursuant to the Customs Law of the People's Republic of China and the Implementing Rules for Customs Administrative Penalties of the People's Republic of China, Gongbei Customs determined that Cai Zengxiong, without legal documentation, had transported a large quantity of foreign cigarettes into internal waters, and such conduct constituted smuggling. Accordingly, it imposed the following penalty decision: 1. The seized 4,760 cases of smuggled cigarettes are to be confiscated; 2. The entire crew of the "Guangda No. 2", the vessel itself, and the loaded porcelain clay and scrap iron are to be released.

Cai Zengxiong, dissatisfied with the penalty decision of Gongbei Customs, filed a lawsuit with the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court. After public trial, the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court held that the vessel "Guangda No. 2" driven by the plaintiff, carrying a large quantity of cigarettes in China's internal waters without legal documentation, should be dealt with as smuggling under the Customs Law. The penalty decision made by Gongbei Customs was supported by solid evidence, based on legal grounds, and followed lawful procedures. On August 17, 1989, the court rendered a judgment to uphold the administrative penalty decision of Gongbei Customs and rejected the plaintiff's claims.

Cai Zengxiong, dissatisfied with the judgment of the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court, filed an appeal with the Guangdong High People's Court. He alleged that the location where the "Guangda No. 2" was intercepted by the customs anti-smuggling vessel was not within the internal waters of the People's Republic of China, and that the cigarettes carried had legal documentation. He requested that the original judgment and the penalty decision of Gongbei Customs be reversed, and that the appellee be ordered to bear the litigation costs of both instances and the lawyer fees and other related expenses incurred by the appellant for the litigation. The appellee Gongbei Customs responded, arguing that the location where the "Guangda No. 2" was seized was within China's internal waters, as evidenced by the navigation chart marked in the appellant's own handwriting; that the "Guangda No. 2" carried a large quantity of foreign cigarettes without any legal documentation; and requested that the original penalty decision and the first-instance judgment be upheld.

The Guangdong High People's Court held upon trial that the location where the appellee Gongbei Customs seized the "Guangda No. 2" was within China's internal waters. The diagrams and records of the positioning of the interception measured by Gongbei Customs' anti-smuggling vessel, signed by the appellant Cai Zengxiong, and the interception location and time marked by Cai Zengxiong himself in pencil on the navigation chart at the time of interception, all proved that the vessel was seized within China's internal waters at longitude 114°35′45″ east and latitude 22°10′50″ north. With respect to the appellant's claim that the large quantity of foreign cigarettes carried by the "Guangda No. 2" had a "Hong Kong Government Export License", upon investigation, this only proved that the cigarettes were permitted for export by Hong Kong, but could not prove that the vessel's loading and transportation were lawful. The cargo manifest of the "Guangda No. 2" had no record of carrying cigarettes at all. Pursuant to Article 49, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Customs Law of the People's Republic of China, transporting, purchasing, or selling goods or articles whose import or export is restricted by the state within internal waters or the territorial sea, in relatively large quantities and without legal documentation, shall be deemed as smuggling according to Item (2) of Paragraph 1 of Article 4 of the Implementing Rules for Customs Administrative Penalties of the People's Republic of China, and the customs authority has the power to confiscate the smuggled goods. The appellant Cai Zengxiong's grounds for appeal cannot be established. The original judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. Accordingly, on December 15, 1989, the Guangdong High People's Court rendered the following judgment: The appeal of the appellant Cai Zengxiong is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.
